purpose: Runtime voice discovery, operator-constrained narrator shortlist, and the equal-condition preview pack presented for explicit operator approval.

runtimeDiscovery.espeak: espeak-ng.dll via espeakng_loader (no manual PATH entry required on Windows)
runtimeDiscovery.installAuthority: explicit operator authorization; providers/local/SETUP_KOKORO.md forbids UNFOLDIQ auto-install
runtimeDiscovery.mechanism: KPipeline.load_single_voice() resolves any voice id at synthesis time via huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download(repo_id, 'voices/<id>.pt'). Kokoro ships NO static voice inventory, so the package directory is not a source of truth.
runtimeDiscovery.repoIdSource: read from the runtime itself (KPipeline.repo_id), not hardcoded here
runtimeDiscovery.verificationRule: a voice is reported usable only after the runtime actually loaded it via load_voice(); enumeration alone would only prove the file is published
runtimeDiscovery.notAsserted: the 54 ids are the upstream repo listing this runtime can resolve; per-voice audio quality is not asserted by discovery

languageCompatibility.adapterCodeNote: python -m kokoro accepts only single-letter lang codes (a,b,h,e,f,i,p,j,z); providers/runtime/adapters/local-kokoro.js now maps en-us -> a. Passing 'en-us' made argparse exit 2, which the adapter previously misread as 'CLI unavailable'.
languageCompatibility.candidatePool: the 20 American English voices (11 af_*, 9 am_*) of the 54-voice inventory

operatorConstraints.rationale: the UNFOLDIQ mascot is male, so narrator identity should remain male to keep brand identity coherent
operatorConstraints.escapeHatch: narrator and mascot may be explicitly decoupled in a later decision; this constraint is a selection input, not a permanent law
operatorConstraints.recordedIn: this evidence document (decision rationale), not a new schema field
operatorConstraints.schemaNote: schemas/voice-bible.schema.json sets additionalProperties:false and has no gender/mascot property. No field was added: the Kokoro voiceId prefix (am_ = American Male, af_ = American Female) already encodes gender deterministically and is validated by the adapter catalog, so a parallel gender field would be redundant state that can disagree with the voiceId.
operatorConstraints.effect: the female candidates af_heart / af_bella / af_nicole / af_kore are WITHDRAWN from the active shortlist despite af_heart having the best official data grade of any en-us voice. Data quality did not override the operator's brand constraint.

shortlist.selectionBasis: Active shortlist is restricted to American English MALE voices (am_*) by the operator's mascot constraint, then narrowed by the official VOICES.md per-voice grades (target quality / training duration / overall grade) as a proxy for consistency and clarity on sustained narration, filtered against the narrator persona's prohibitedTraits (no announcer bombast, no overacting, no robotic clause rhythm).

officialDataSource.sourceNote: The RAW resolve/main markdown was used. An earlier pass read the HTML-rendered model page, whose table columns silently misaligned for several rows and produced wrong grades for am_michael, am_puck, am_onyx and af_sky. The operator caught this; the raw file is authoritative.

wrongEarlierValues.am_puck: was recorded as Target Quality C / MM minutes / Grade D; official is B / H hours / C+
wrongEarlierValues.am_onyx: was recorded as Target Quality B / MM minutes / Grade C; official is C / MM minutes / D
wrongEarlierValues.af_sky: was recorded as Target Quality C / M minutes / Grade C-; official is B / M minutes / C-

gradeCorrection.consequence: All three shortlisted male voices are EQUAL on official evidence (B / H hours / C+). The earlier rationale that ranked am_fenrir above am_michael and am_puck 'on data' was unfounded and has been withdrawn. Selection is now a pure timbre/brand judgement, not a data judgement.
gradeCorrection.operatorInstruction: shortlist held at exactly am_fenrir, am_michael, am_puck; am_onyx confirmed lower (C / MM minutes / D), consistent with the operator's own reading.

voices.notes: On official evidence am_fenrir is NOT better supported than the other two - all three are B / H hours / C+. Its distinguishing measured properties are the highest median pitch (133.3 Hz) and the widest pitch spread (40.1%).
Operator-requested addition. Official grade EQUALS the other two. Measured: quietest of the set (RMS -27.36 dBFS, ~5 dB below am_fenrir) and lowest pitch spread (28.6%).

Operator-requested addition. Official grade EQUALS the other two. Measured: hottest/loudest (peak -1.45 dBFS, only 1.45 dB of headroom) and lowest pitch (110.1 Hz). Hottest peak is worth noting for 2.4 loudness QA.

objectiveQaMetrics.basis: every value measured from the rendered WAV (headers + samples); nothing estimated or copied from documentation
objectiveQaMetrics.whyTheseMetrics: the narrator persona's prohibitedTraits are partly measurable, so ear-only description is not evidence: EXCESSIVE_PAUSES -> longestInternalPauseSec/speechRatio, UNNATURALLY_SLOW_CINEMATIC -> speakingRateWpm, MONOTONE_CADENCE -> energyCv, ANNOUNCER_BOMBAST -> peakDbfs/rmsDbfs. Pitch metrics give objective timbre identity and consistency.
objectiveQaMetrics.NOTAJudgement: these metrics do not rank voices and imply no quality verdict; approval remains an explicit human decision
observations: Speaking rate is effectively identical across the three (197-203 wpm against active speech), so no speedDefault compensation is needed and the earlier am_michael '~14% slower' concern is resolved - the raw duration gap (6.125s vs 5.375s) is mostly leading/trailing silence, not slower speech.
No voice shows an internal pause at all (longestInternalPauseSec = 0.0), so EXCESSIVE_PAUSES is not a differentiator.
All three are in the expected male band (110-133 Hz median F0), consistent with the mascot-male constraint.
am_puck peaks at -1.45 dBFS, i.e. only 1.45 dB of headroom. Harmless for a preview but it is the one voice that could clip if 2.4 pushes loudness normalisation.
am_michael is ~5 dB quieter than the others at RMS, so a perceived-level difference is expected when switching between them.

previewPack.classificationNote: Selection scratch, not durable evidence and not production narration.
previewPack.equalConditionGuarantee: All three active candidates were rendered in a SINGLE batch through one buildPreviewPack() call, so script, speed, language, format and code path are provably identical. Durations are therefore comparable without caveat.

sharedInvariants.sampleText: Kokoro is an open weight text to speech model with eighty two million parameters.

previewPack.measurementNote: Durations and RMS were measured from the rendered WAV headers and samples, not estimated. Every file is a real RIFF/24kHz/16-bit stream with non-silent RMS, so none fell through the adapter's silent-audio fallback path.

withdrawnCandidatesRetained.note: The female previews remain on disk as RETENTION_MANAGED scratch in case the narrator/mascot coupling is explicitly decoupled later; they are not part of the active shortlist.

approvalState.autoSelection: none - there is no default, no scoring shortcut and no auto-select path in lib/voice-bible/license.js, and none in the QA tool
approvalState.priorDecision: The operator reviewed a 5-voice mixed shortlist and declined to approve, citing the male-mascot constraint. No voice has been approved at any point in this FIX.

technicalRecommendationIssued.explicitlyNotAnApproval: A technical recommendation was produced and presented. The operator decision remains OUTSTANDING; nothing was persisted as a selection, no Voice Bible version was created, and the manifest is unchanged.
